## Use this as a skill, not just a demo

Install the Narrative Deck skill in your AI assistant, then ask it to use narrative-deck before building. The skill helps your agent choose the right story beats, place effects with restraint, and keep the page dependency-free.

Before the effects

## The Structural Frame

Fifteen techniques are useless without a skeleton to hang them on. This is the beat sequence underneath a premium article — nine positions, each with a job. Click any beat to see what belongs there and which effects serve it.

### —

Effect 01

## Scroll-Triggered Reveal

Elements stay invisible until they enter the viewport, then fade and rise into place. An IntersectionObserver watches each block and adds a class — no scroll listener, no jank.

Panel one arrives first.

Panel two follows at 180 ms.

Panel three closes the sequence.

Effect 02

## Sticky Scrollytelling

A city map pins to the viewport while text panels scroll past it. Each panel pans, zooms, or labels the same map — the scroll becomes a guided investigation.

Effect 03

## Hover Disclosure

Detail lives one gesture away. Hover reveals hidden content without cluttering the default view.

Effect 04

## “You Draw It” Canvas

Drag across the blank half of the chart to predict the trend. Release, then reveal the truth.

Effect 05

## Physics Field (Canvas)

Orbs with a simple physics simulation respond to the cursor. The same engine can push body text aside in magazine-style layouts.

Effect 06

## Forensic Annotation & Scrubber

Pins teach the reader how to look . The timeline slider replays the decisive seconds.

Effect 07

## Kinetic Type & Highlight Wipe

Characters animate in sequence; a key phrase fills with colour as it scrolls into view.

Attention is earned per scroll.

The strongest sentence gets a colour wipe instead of bold — slower, and therefore noticed.

Effect 08

## Parallax Depth

Six layers translate at different rates against the scroll. Distant layers barely move; near layers move most, which the brain reads as physical depth.

Effect 09

## Color-Threaded Entities

A colour introduced in prose reappears in every chart, map and timeline that follows. The reader builds a private visual vocabulary and never needs a legend.

Three districts reported sharply different outcomes. Northfield recovered fastest, while Lakeside stalled by midyear. Eastgate never regained its baseline at all.

Effect 10

## Binary Quiz Accumulator

Twelve statements, one tap each. Lowering the cost of a single interaction is what lets you raise the number of interactions.

Effect 11

## Turn-by-Turn Procedural Graphic

One continuous action, decomposed into five inspectable phases. The reader can watch it run, or stop and interrogate any single stage.

Effect 12

## AR Placeholder — Spatial Artifact Viewer

A 3D object you inspect by tilting your phone or dragging on desktop. Annotation hotspots surface context when you rotate the artifact to face them.

Effect 13

## Before / After Comparison

A draggable divider between two states of the same scene. The reader performs the comparison rather than being told the conclusion.

Effect 14

## Audio Waveform & Transcript Sync

A scrubable waveform bound to a transcript. Clicking any line jumps the playhead; the active line highlights as it plays.

Effect 15

## Dynamic Paywall Simulator

The most consequential storytelling effect is invisible: a model deciding where in your reading journey the narrative gets interrupted. Adjust the reader profile and watch the meter move.
